# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format is based on
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project
adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Releases are cut from `vX.Y.Z` Git tags; pushing a tag publishes the matching
Docker images to GHCR (see [docs/OPERATIONS.md](docs/OPERATIONS.md)).

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- Custom statistics widgets now honor the “All linked trees” scope, including
  readable linked trees only and counting bridge persons once (#570).
- The in-app changelog now renders release notes in small, on-demand windows,
  avoiding a full-history Markdown render as releases accumulate (#746).
- The in-app changelog is now generated from this source file while every
  frontend image is built, so published images cannot display a stale committed
  copy (#745).
- The gallery upload progress panel now dismisses itself automatically once
  every image has uploaded successfully, instead of lingering after the uploads
  complete. It stays open when an upload fails so the failure can be reviewed
  and retried (#731).

### Added

- The tree-view people search now shows current-tree matches first, then
  searches every other tree shared with the user; selecting an outside match
  opens and centers that person in its tree (#724).
- Live collaboration presence: avatar chips in the tree canvas show who else is
  currently viewing the open tree — including yourself and accepted friends
  with profile pictures, and other collaborators with initials/icon fallbacks —
  once another person joins, and highlight anyone editing; a member sheet also
  shows an indicator when someone else has it open in edit mode.
  Backed by heartbeats with TTL expiry, works single-worker (in-process) and
  multi-worker (`REDIS_URL`), and is gated behind a new admin-toggleable
  `presence` feature flag (#723).
- Friends can now see an accepted friend's profile picture in the Friends view;
  images continue to be served through an authenticated friendship-only route
  (#739).
- The Statistics view now has an “On this day” widget for upcoming birthdays,
  death anniversaries, dated events, and stories, with direct links to people
  in the tree (#727).
- Generation lines can now be adjusted per tree from the sidebar with None and
  four snap-aligned spacing presets, while preserving node-center alignment
  (#743).
- Linking a person who is already attached to a gallery image now confirms that
  existing link instead of failing without feedback (#728).
- Gallery images opened from a member's detail view now show linked people and
  their face-tag regions (#728).
- Uploading photos from a member's edit view now opens face tagging for each
  new image, so a face can be marked immediately (#728).
- Users can now set first and last profile names and select an adjustable crop
  when uploading, replacing, or removing a private profile picture. Account
  avatars consistently prefer the picture, then name initials, then a generic
  user icon (#737).
- Gallery photos can now be annotated with manual, normalized face regions
  linked to people in the tree. Face tags remain accurate at every display
  size, and existing whole-image links continue to work unchanged (#728).

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    tags:
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

# Cancel superseded in-progress runs on the same PR. Never cancel push/tag
# runs — those publish container images and must run to completion.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  # Detect which areas a PR touched so the irrelevant heavy jobs can be skipped.
  # On push/tag we always run everything (full validation before publishing).
  changes:
    name: "Detect changed areas"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      frontend: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.frontend }}
      backend: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.backend }}
    steps:
      - name: "Checkout Code"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Filter changed paths"
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            frontend:
              - 'frontend/**'
              - '.github/workflows/check-build.yml'
            backend:
              - 'backend/**'
              - '.github/workflows/check-build.yml'

  frontend:
    name: "Frontend (build + test + i18n)"
    needs: changes
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.frontend == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - name: "Checkout Code"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Set up Node.js"
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: "Install dependencies"
        run: npm ci

      - name: "Type-check & build"
        run: npm run build

      - name: "Bundle size budget"
        run: npm run check-bundle-size

      - name: "Unit tests"
        run: npx vitest run

      - name: "Translation parity"
        run: npm run check-i18n

      - name: "No explicit any"
        run: npm run check-no-any

  i18n-status:
    # Compatibility status for existing branch protection. The actual
    # `npm run check-i18n` command runs in the frontend job above.
    name: "Check for Missing i18n Keys"
    needs: [frontend]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: "Require frontend i18n step to pass"
        run: |
          res="${{ needs.frontend.result }}"
          echo "frontend=$res"
          # "skipped" means the PR touched no frontend files — nothing to check.
          if [ "$res" != "success" ] && [ "$res" != "skipped" ]; then
            echo "The frontend job runs npm run check-i18n and did not pass."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "i18n OK (frontend job: $res)."

  backend:
    name: "Backend (deps + checks)"
    needs: changes
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.backend == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      - name: "Checkout Code"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Set up uv"
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: "Install dependencies"
        run: uv sync --frozen

      - name: "Lint (ruff)"
        run: uv run ruff check

      - name: "Compile & import checks"
        run: |
          uv run python -m compileall -q app alembic
          uv run python -c "import app.main; print('app imports OK')"

      - name: "Unit tests"
        # -n auto fans the suite across the runner's cores (pytest-xdist).
        # Tests are isolation-safe: each gets its own SQLite DB via tmp_path.
        run: uv run pytest -n auto

  version-policy:
    name: "Version metadata policy"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: "Checkout Code"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Check package metadata"
        run: |
          PACKAGE_VERSION=$(jq -r .version frontend/package.json)
          LOCK_VERSION=$(jq -r .version frontend/package-lock.json)
          LOCK_ROOT_VERSION=$(jq -r '.packages[""].version' frontend/package-lock.json)
          PYPROJECT_VERSION=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' backend/pyproject.toml | head -1)
          UV_LOCK_VERSION=$(grep -A1 '^name = "family-tree-backend"$' backend/uv.lock | sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p')

          echo "frontend/package.json:      $PACKAGE_VERSION"
          echo "frontend/package-lock.json: $LOCK_VERSION"
          echo "lock root package:          $LOCK_ROOT_VERSION"
          echo "backend/pyproject.toml:     $PYPROJECT_VERSION"
          echo "backend/uv.lock:            $UV_LOCK_VERSION"

          if [ "$PACKAGE_VERSION" != "$LOCK_VERSION" ] || [ "$PACKAGE_VERSION" != "$LOCK_ROOT_VERSION" ] \
            || [ "$PACKAGE_VERSION" != "$PYPROJECT_VERSION" ] || [ "$PACKAGE_VERSION" != "$UV_LOCK_VERSION" ]; then
            echo "Version metadata is out of sync across frontend/backend."
            echo "Run 'npm run bump:patch|minor|major' from frontend/ — it updates all four files."
            exit 1
          fi

          if [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then
            TAG_VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
            echo "Release tag:                $TAG_VERSION"
            if [ "$TAG_VERSION" != "$PACKAGE_VERSION" ] || [ "$TAG_VERSION" != "$LOCK_VERSION" ] \
              || [ "$TAG_VERSION" != "$LOCK_ROOT_VERSION" ] || [ "$TAG_VERSION" != "$PYPROJECT_VERSION" ] \
              || [ "$TAG_VERSION" != "$UV_LOCK_VERSION" ]; then
              echo "Release tag v$TAG_VERSION does not match all release metadata."
              exit 1
            fi
          else
            echo "Ordinary PRs and main pushes do not need a version bump."
          fi

  # Aggregate gate so the existing required status check named
  # "Check Application Build" (branch protection) keeps being reported.
  check-build:
    name: "Check Application Build"
    needs: [changes, frontend, i18n-status, backend, version-policy]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: "Require all checks to pass"
        run: |
          echo "changes=${{ needs.changes.result }} frontend=${{ needs.frontend.result }} i18n-status=${{ needs.i18n-status.result }} backend=${{ needs.backend.result }} version-policy=${{ needs.version-policy.result }}"
          # Change-detection must succeed, else we'd skip everything and pass blindly.
          if [ "${{ needs.changes.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Change detection failed."
            exit 1
          fi
          # frontend/backend may be legitimately "skipped" when their area was untouched.
          for res in "${{ needs.frontend.result }}" "${{ needs.backend.result }}"; do
            if [ "$res" != "success" ] && [ "$res" != "skipped" ]; then
              echo "A build/test job failed ($res)."
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          # The always-on gate jobs must pass outright.
          if [ "${{ needs.i18n-status.result }}" != "success" ] || [ "${{ needs.version-policy.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "A required gate job failed."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All checks passed (skipped = no changes in that area)."

  release-e2e:
    name: "Release Playwright E2E"
    needs: [check-build]
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30

    env:
      E2E_ADMIN_USERNAME: e2e-admin
      E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD: e2e-admin-password
      E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:8080
      E2E_API_URL: http://localhost:8080/api

    steps:
      - name: "Checkout"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Build & start compose stack"
        run: |
          docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml up --build -d
        env:
          E2E_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${{ env.E2E_ADMIN_USERNAME }}
          E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${{ env.E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}

      - name: "Wait for stack to be healthy"
        run: |
          echo "Waiting for frontend to be reachable..."
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf http://localhost:8080 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Stack is up after ${i} attempts"
              break
            fi
            echo "  attempt $i/30 — waiting 5s"
            sleep 5
          done
          curl -sf http://localhost:8080/api/health/ready || {
            echo "Backend health check failed"
            docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml logs
            exit 1
          }

      - name: "Set up Node.js"
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: e2e/package-lock.json

      - name: "Install dependencies"
        working-directory: e2e
        run: npm ci

      - name: "Install Playwright browsers"
        working-directory: e2e
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: "Run Playwright tests"
        working-directory: e2e
        run: npx playwright test
        env:
          E2E_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${{ env.E2E_ADMIN_USERNAME }}
          E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${{ env.E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}
          E2E_BASE_URL: ${{ env.E2E_BASE_URL }}
          E2E_API_URL: ${{ env.E2E_API_URL }}

      - name: "Upload test report"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: release-playwright-report
          path: e2e/playwright-report/
          retention-days: 14

      - name: "Upload traces on failure"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: release-playwright-traces
          path: e2e/test-results/
          retention-days: 7

      - name: "Dump compose logs on failure"
        if: failure()
        run: docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml logs

      - name: "Tear down compose stack"
        if: always()
        run: docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml down -v

  images:
    name: "Build & push ${{ matrix.service }} image"
    needs: [check-build, release-e2e]
    if: |
      always() &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.check-build.result == 'success' &&
      (!startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || needs.release-e2e.result == 'success')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    concurrency:
      group: publish-images-${{ github.ref }}-${{ matrix.service }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - service: backend
            context: ./backend
            dockerfile: ./backend/Dockerfile
          - service: frontend
            context: .
            dockerfile: ./frontend/Dockerfile

    steps:
      - name: "Checkout Code"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Resolve build metadata"
        id: build-meta
        run: |
          SHORT_SHA="${GITHUB_SHA::7}"
          if [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then
            VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          elif [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/heads/* ]]; then
            REF_NAME="${GITHUB_REF_NAME//\//-}"
            VERSION="${REF_NAME}-${SHORT_SHA}"
          else
            VERSION="manual-${SHORT_SHA}"
          fi

          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "revision=$GITHUB_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "build_date=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: "Log in to GHCR"
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: "Docker metadata"
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v6
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}-${{ matrix.service }}
          flavor: latest=false
          tags: |
            type=ref,event=branch
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') }}
            type=sha,format=short

      - name: "Set up Docker Buildx"
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      # Build into the local Docker daemon first so Trivy can scan the image
      # before anything is pushed. The push step below is a pure cache hit.
      - name: "Build for scanning"
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: ${{ matrix.context }}
          file: ${{ matrix.dockerfile }}
          load: true
          tags: scan-target/${{ matrix.service }}:ci
          build-args: |
            APP_VERSION=${{ steps.build-meta.outputs.version }}
            APP_REVISION=${{ steps.build-meta.outputs.revision }}
            APP_BUILD_DATE=${{ steps.build-meta.outputs.build_date }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

      - name: "Report vulnerabilities (Trivy)"
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0.36.0
        with:
          image-ref: scan-target/${{ matrix.service }}:ci
          format: table
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          exit-code: "0"

      - name: "Gate on fixable CRITICAL vulnerabilities (Trivy)"
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0.36.0
        with:
          image-ref: scan-target/${{ matrix.service }}:ci
          format: table
          severity: CRITICAL
          # Only fixable CRITICALs block the publish; a CVE with no patched
          # package available yet shouldn't stall releases.
          ignore-unfixed: true
          exit-code: "1"
          skip-setup-trivy: true

      - name: "Build and push"
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: ${{ matrix.context }}
          file: ${{ matrix.dockerfile }}
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          build-args: |
            APP_VERSION=${{ steps.build-meta.outputs.version }}
            APP_REVISION=${{ steps.build-meta.outputs.revision }}
            APP_BUILD_DATE=${{ steps.build-meta.outputs.build_date }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

name: Security Scan

# Dependency vulnerability scanning for both dependency trees. Dependency Review
# blocks newly introduced critical vulnerable dependencies in PRs; the broader
# npm/pip audits stay report-only so existing baseline noise remains visible
# without blocking routine work.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  schedule:
    # Weekly, Monday 05:00 UTC - catches advisories published between PRs.
    - cron: "0 5 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

# Cancel superseded scans on the same PR; leave scheduled/dispatch runs alone.
# No path filtering here: dependency-review may be a required check, and a
# workflow-level path skip would leave it permanently pending and block merges.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  dependency-review:
    name: "Dependency Review"
    # Dependency review requires the dependency graph + GitHub Advanced Security, which private personal repos don't have.
    if: ${{ !github.event.repository.private && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: "Checkout Code"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Review dependency changes"
        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v5
        with:
          fail-on-severity: critical

  npm-audit:
    name: "Frontend (npm audit)"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - name: "Checkout Code"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Set up Node.js"
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: "Audit production dependencies"
        # Report-only: surface the report in the job summary, don't fail the PR.
        run: |
          echo '## npm audit (production deps)' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          npm audit --omit=dev | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  pip-audit:
    name: "Backend (pip-audit)"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      - name: "Checkout Code"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: "Set up uv"
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: "Audit locked dependencies"
        # Audit exactly what uv.lock pins for production (no dev group).
        # Report-only: surface the report in the job summary, don't fail the PR.
        run: |
          uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes \
            --format requirements-txt -o requirements-audit.txt
          echo '## pip-audit (locked production deps)' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          uvx pip-audit --requirement requirements-audit.txt --no-deps --disable-pip \
            | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

I dug through the four workflows, the bump/changelog scripts, and the in-app changelog wiring. Here's what I'd change, in priority order.

## 1. The core gap: there is no release workflow

Today a release is a human running `npm run release:minor` locally and pushing a tag; [check-build.yml](.github/workflows/check-build.yml) reacts to the tag, runs E2E, and pushes images — but **no GitHub Release is ever created**. So `docs/OPERATIONS.md` tells self-hosters to pin `APP_IMAGE_TAG=1.2.17` while the Releases page stays empty.

A `workflow_dispatch` release job fixes both that and your manual-trigger ask.

**The gotcha that decides the design:** a tag pushed using `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` does **not** trigger other workflows. So a naive "bump + tag + push, let check-build.yml catch it" release will bump and then silently publish nothing.

Two ways out — I'd take the second:

- **A.** Push the tag with a GitHub App token (`actions/create-github-app-token@v2`) so the tag event fires normally. Works, but you're now depending on the token's trigger semantics, and the release run and the tag run are separate.
- **B. (recommended)** Extract the reusable pieces of `check-build.yml` into `on: workflow_call` workflows — `checks.yml` (frontend/backend/version) and `publish-images.yml` (the matrix + Trivy + push) — and have `release.yml` call them directly. The release becomes one linear, observable run: **verify → bump → tag → E2E → publish images → create GitHub Release**. `GITHUB_TOKEN` is enough, and you get no duplicate tag-triggered build.

Sketch:

```yaml
name: Release
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        type: boolean
        default: false
permissions: { contents: write, packages: write }
concurrency: { group: release, cancel-in-progress: false }
```

Details worth building in:

- **Guard on `main`**: fail fast if `github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'`.
- **Re-run the full checks on the bump commit**, don't just query whether main was green — the release commit is new content, and `checks.yml` is cheap relative to a bad release.
- **`dry_run`**: do everything, upload the computed version + generated notes as a job-summary artifact, skip push/tag/publish. Makes the whole thing safe to test.
- **Attach `docker-compose.prod.yml` + `.env.example` as release assets** — a real convenience for self-hosters landing on the Releases page.
- **Branch protection**: if `main` is protected, the release commit push needs a GitHub App token or a bypass allowance for the app. Worth deciding up front.
- **Option worth considering:** make the **tag the single source of truth** and stop syncing four files. Compute the next version from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` instead of `frontend/package.json`, leave the in-repo versions at a `0.0.0-dev` placeholder, and the entire `version-policy` job + [check-version.yml](.github/workflows/check-version.yml) become unnecessary. Bigger change, but it deletes a whole class of "metadata out of sync" failures.

## 2. Changelog generated from commits

Your commit subjects on `main` are already ideal input — squash merges with Conventional Commits prefixes and a trailing `(#PR)`:

```
feat(activity): single-action undo for logged deletes (#819)
fix(sharing): surface revoked tree access to open sessions (#813, #814) (#818)
```

**Use [git-cliff](https://git-cliff.org)** (`orhun/git-cliff-action@v4`). Single Rust binary, no npm dependency in the release path, template-driven, and it does exactly the "commits since the last tag" range you asked for:

```bash
git cliff --unreleased --tag "v$NEW_VERSION" --output RELEASE_NOTES.md   # notes for this release
git cliff --tag "v$NEW_VERSION" --output CHANGELOG.md                    # full regenerated file
```

A `cliff.toml` maps prefixes to sections — `feat` → Added, `fix` → Fixed, `perf`/`refactor` → Changed, and `skip = true` for `chore(deps)`, `test`, `docs`, `typing` (that last one matters: your recent `typing:` series would otherwise flood the notes).

Alternatives I considered and would not pick here:

- **release-please** — automates more (it maintains a release PR), but you asked for a manual trigger, and it would need custom updaters to touch `backend/uv.lock`. Fights your existing `bump-version.js`.
- **GitHub's built-in auto-generated notes** (`generate_release_notes: true` + `.github/release.yml`) — zero dependencies, but categorizes by **PR label**, not commit prefix, so you'd have to start labeling consistently. Decent fallback; weaker than git-cliff given your commit hygiene.

**One honest trade-off:** your hand-written `## [Unreleased]` entries are considerably richer than commit subjects — compare *"The gallery upload progress panel now dismisses itself automatically once every image has uploaded successfully…"* against `fix(gallery): dismiss upload panel`. Generated notes will be terser. Two mitigations: configure git-cliff to include commit *bodies* for `feat`/`fix`, and add a **PR-title lint** job (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`) — since you squash-merge, the PR title *is* the changelog line, so that's where the quality gate belongs.

Then drop the "must add a CHANGELOG entry" rule from [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), the PR checklist, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Either delete `CHANGELOG.md` entirely (Releases become the record) or let the release job regenerate and commit it — I'd keep a generated copy, it costs nothing and helps people browsing the repo.

## 3. Removing the in-app changelog

Full inventory of what this touches:

**Delete:** `frontend/src/components/changelog/` (all 5 files), [useWhatsNewStore.ts](frontend/src/hooks/useWhatsNewStore.ts), [gen-changelog.mjs](frontend/scripts/gen-changelog.mjs), `parse-changelog.mjs` + its test, `frontend/src/data/changelog.json` (+ its gitignore entry), [version.ts](frontend/src/utils/version.ts) (only exists for changelog display).

**Edit:** remove the `predev`/`prebuild` hooks and `gen-changelog` script from `frontend/package.json`; drop `<WhatsNewAnnouncementDialog />` from [Layout.tsx:29](frontend/src/components/layout/Layout.tsx:29); drop the changelog tab from [UserSettingsView.tsx:196](frontend/src/components/settings/UserSettingsView.tsx:196); remove the `changelog.*` keys from `en.json` and `de.json`; clean the `useWhatsNewStore` references in `App.tsx` and `MainPanel.tsx`.

**Backend:** the whats-new endpoints in [preferences.py:97](backend/app/api/routes/preferences.py:97) and `WhatsNewState` in `schemas/user.py`. No migration needed — `whats_new_last_read_version` lives inside the JSON prefs blob, so a stale key just goes unread.

**The version link:** [FamilyTreeSidebar.tsx:87](frontend/src/components/sidebar/FamilyTreeSidebar.tsx:87) currently renders `v{APP_VERSION}` as a dialog trigger. Make it an external link to `https://github.com/maxi-smidt/family-tree/releases/tag/v{APP_VERSION}` — but branch on it: `APP_VERSION` is `dev` locally and `main-<sha>` for branch builds ([buildInfo.ts](frontend/src/lib/buildInfo.ts)), and those tags don't exist. Link non-release builds to `/releases` instead, or the badge 404s for anyone building from source.

## 4. Other things I'd fix

Ranked by what I'd actually do first:

1. **Multi-arch images.** You build amd64 only. For a self-hostable app that's a real limitation — Raspberry Pi and Apple Silicon users can't run your images. Add `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64` on tag builds. Note this interacts with your scan-then-push pattern: `load: true` can't load a multi-platform result, so scan the amd64 image, then push multi-arch (or split into per-platform build jobs + a merge job).
2. **`alembic check` against real Postgres.** Your pytest suite runs on SQLite, so PG-specific migration behavior is never exercised, and model changes without a migration aren't caught. A job with a `postgres` service that runs `alembic upgrade head` then `alembic check` (fails when autogenerate would produce a diff) directly enforces the rule in AGENTS.md that CI currently can't see.
3. **Delete [check-version.yml](.github/workflows/check-version.yml).** Its logic is duplicated verbatim by the `version-policy` job inside `check-build.yml`. Two workflows, one purpose — and it's the *weaker* copy (no tag check). Repoint branch protection at the `version-policy` name and drop the file.
4. **Post-publish smoke test.** `release-e2e` tests a stack built from source, then you push separately built images. Nothing verifies the *published* artifacts. After the images job, pull `ghcr.io/...:$VERSION`, bring up the prod compose file, hit `/api/health/ready`. Catches broken build args and bad layers before users do.
5. **Supply chain**: add `provenance: mode=max` + `sbom: true` to the build-push action, and `actions/attest-build-provenance`. Cheap, and for a self-hosted app it's a meaningful trust signal. **CodeQL** for JS/TS + Python too, if the repo is public.
6. **GHCR retention.** Every push to main leaves a `sha-xxxxxxx` tag forever. A monthly `actions/delete-package-versions` job keeping the last ~30 untagged versions prevents the package page rotting.
7. **`timeout-minutes` on every job.** Only `release-e2e` has one; a hung frontend job currently burns 6 hours.
8. **Tighten the `workflow_dispatch` publish condition.** In the `images` job, `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` lets a manual run publish images **from any branch**. Add a ref guard.

Want me to implement any of these? I'd suggest starting with the reusable-workflow refactor + `release.yml` + git-cliff as one PR, and the in-app changelog removal as a second, since the latter touches i18n, the backend, and tests.

## Point 5 — supply chain, explained

Three separate things I bundled too tightly last time. The repo is **public**, so all of this is free.

**Build provenance attestation.** `actions/attest-build-provenance` produces a Sigstore-signed SLSA statement bound to the image *digest*, recording which repo, workflow file, commit SHA, and runner produced it. Keyless — the signing identity comes from the runner's OIDC token, so there's nothing to rotate or leak. A self-hoster can then run:

```bash
gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/maxi-smidt/family-tree-backend:1.8.0 --repo maxi-smidt/family-tree
```

That answers "was this image really built from that repo's `main`, or did someone with a leaked GHCR token push it?" — a question that currently has no answer. Needs `id-token: write` + `attestations: write` permissions; adds ~30s.

There's a second, overlapping mechanism: `docker/build-push-action`'s `provenance: mode=max`, which writes BuildKit's own in-toto attestations into the registry as extra manifest entries. Same idea, different plumbing — and a real caveat: it turns a single-manifest image into an index with attestation manifests, which some older registry mirrors and tooling handle poorly. I'd take the GitHub attestation route and leave BuildKit provenance off.

**SBOM.** A machine-readable inventory (SPDX or CycloneDX) of every OS and language package inside the image. Trivy already scans at build time — but that's a snapshot against the vulnerability DB *as it existed that day*. The SBOM is what lets you answer, six months later when the next xz-style advisory drops, "is the affected package in v1.8.0?" without rebuilding a possibly-unreproducible image. Attach it as a release asset, or attest it with `actions/attest-sbom`. Adds ~1 min per image.

**CodeQL.** This is the one I'd argue hardest for, because it covers a gap nothing else does. Your entire [security-scan.yml](.github/workflows/security-scan.yml) — npm audit, pip-audit, dependency-review — scans *other people's code*. Nothing statically analyzes yours. CodeQL does taint tracking across JS/TS and Python: path traversal, SSRF, SQL injection, unsafe deserialization, XSS. Given this app writes uploads to `DATA_PATH/media`, parses GEDCOM files, does encrypted export/import bundles, and enforces per-tree authorization on every content query, path traversal on media paths is a realistic finding class. Free and unlimited on public repos. Cost is runtime: ~5–10 min per language, so PR-triggered on changed languages plus a weekly full scan. Start with the default query suite — `security-extended` is noticeably noisier.

`docker/metadata-action` emits `type=sha,format=short` on every push, so each merge to `main` creates two new image versions (`sha-abc1234` for backend and frontend) that nothing ever removes. At your recent merge rate that's roughly 80 image versions a month, forever. Separately, every time the moving `main` and `latest` tags re-point, the version they *used* to point at becomes an untagged orphan.

I should correct the emphasis from my earlier list: **for a public repo, GHCR storage and bandwidth are free**, so this is not a cost problem. It's a discoverability and hygiene one — the public package page becomes a wall of `sha-` tags that buries the actual releases someone came looking for.

Two ways to fix it, and the cheaper one is worth considering first:

- **Stop creating the garbage.** Drop or narrow `type=sha` in the metadata action. If nobody actually deploys from `sha-` tags, they're pure noise and the retention job becomes unnecessary.
- **Clean up on a schedule.** `actions/delete-package-versions` monthly. This directory contains issue templates optimized for GitHub Copilot agents and human contributors.

### 🐛 Bug Report (`bug_report.yml`)
Use this template to report bugs or unexpected behavior in the Family Tree application.

**Key Features:**
- Structured fields for bug description, reproduction steps, and expected behavior
- Environment information collection (OS, version, database)
- Error logs and console output sections
- Relevant file/component identification
- Screenshot/video support
- Pre-submission checklist

- Dedicated "Relevant Files/Components" section helps Copilot locate code quickly

- Clear expected vs. actual behavior helps Copilot understand the issue
